proofs.proof_tex:
The established uniform-risk theorem gives totality of \(\delta_n^\star\) and
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\le\max_y\mathbb E[(\delta_n^\star-\tau_c(y))^2]
\le n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}.
\tag{13}
\]
Here the first inequality is the minimax definition.  That theorem also verifies \(q_a^\star>0\) on \(S_c\); inactive labels have probability zero and the procedure has its stated total fallback.

The full-label Bayes converse says that for every rational \(\eta>0\), eventually
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\ge n^{-1}-(\Lambda_c+\eta)n^{-4/3}.
\tag{14}
\]
For
\[
e_n=n^{4/3}\left[R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
-\{n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}\}\right],
\]
(13)--(14) give \(-\eta\le e_n\le B_cn^{-1/6}\) eventually.  Given real \(\epsilon>0\), choose rational \(0<\eta<\epsilon\) and then \(n\) large enough that (14) holds and \(B_cn^{-1/6}<\epsilon\).  Hence \(|e_n|<\epsilon\), proving
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{15}
\]

Let \(\mathfrak D_n^\star\) be the singleton product-law class with probabilities \(q^\star\).  By the zero-sum and \(\ell_1\)-normalization assumptions, the positive coefficients of \(c\) sum to one and the negative coefficients sum to minus one.  Hence every binary target belongs to \([-1,1]\).  Projecting any real-valued action onto \([-1,1]\) weakly reduces its distance from every such target, so the binary specialization of the new game satisfies
\[
R_{n,\{0,1\}}^{\mathfrak D^\star}(c)=R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c).
\tag{16}
\]
Apply the bounded-endpoint reduction to \(\mathfrak D_n^\star\).  The required zero-sum condition is already verified, and fixed \(L<U\) gives a finite positive scale.  Its exact equality and (16) give
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
=(U-L)^2R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c).
\tag{17}
\]
Substitution of (15) proves the bounded expansion, since fixed multiplication preserves the little-order remainder.  Finally use \(\delta_n^\star\) as the binary input to the explicit construction (6)--(7) in the reduction lemma.  Its inequality (10) and (13) show that the resulting observable total estimator \(\delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star\) has maximum risk at most
\[
(U-L)^2\{n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}\}.
\tag{18}
\]
This proves every binary and bounded clause with no oracle observation and no assumption that a minimax infimum is attained.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every fixed \(K\ge3\), every \(n\ge1\), every fixed real pair \(L<U\), every contrast satisfying \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_a=0\), and every nonempty class \(\mathfrak D_n\) of outcome-independent assignment laws,
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathfrak D}(c)
=(U-L)^2R_{n,\{0,1\}}^{\mathfrak D}(c).
\]
This finite-sample equality preserves the design-law class, permits arbitrary dependence among unit assignments, and permits arbitrary possibly randomized, biased labeled-data estimators.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Set \(d=U-L>0\).  For \(y\in[L,U]^{n\times K}\), put \(z_{i,a}=(y_{i,a}-L)/d\).  Then \(z\in[0,1]^{n\times K}\), and the zero-sum assumption gives
\[
\tau_c(y)=\frac1n\sum_{i,a}c_a\{L+dz_{i,a}\}
=d\frac1n\sum_{i,a}c_az_{i,a}=d\tau_c(z).
\tag{1}
\]
The positivity of \(d\) justifies every division.

For the lower bound, embed a binary schedule \(b\) as \(y^b=L+db\).  Given a design \(\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D_n\) and an interval estimator \(\widehat\tau_I\), define
\[
\widehat\tau_{01}(A,b_A)
=d^{-1}\widehat\tau_I(A,L+db_A).
\tag{2}
\]
The endpoint data on the right are computable from \((A,b_A)\).  Equation (1) gives pointwise
\[
\{\widehat\tau_I-\tau_c(y^b)\}^2
=d^2\{\widehat\tau_{01}-\tau_c(b)\}^2.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus every interval procedure has maximum risk at least \(d^2\) times the optimal binary maximum risk under its same design.  Taking the estimator and then design infima yields
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathfrak D}(c)
\ge d^2R_{n,\{0,1\}}^{\mathfrak D}(c).
\tag{4}
\]

For the reverse bound, fix \(\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D_n\) and a binary procedure \(\widehat\tau_{01}\).  Projection onto \([ -\|c\|_1/2,\|c\|_1/2]\), which contains every zero-sum binary target, cannot increase squared error, so take this procedure bounded.  Conditional on the fixed \(z\), draw mutually independent latent cells
\[
\Xi_{i,a}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(z_{i,a}),
\tag{5}
\]
independently of the assignment and procedure randomization, and set
\[
\widehat\tau_I(A,y_A)
=d\,\mathbb E_{\Xi,\widehat\tau_{01}}
[\widehat\tau_{01}(A,\Xi_A)\mid A,y_A].
\tag{6}
\]
If \(m(A,x)\) is the mean action of the binary Markov kernel at \((A,x)\), then
\[
\widehat\tau_I(A,y_A)
=d\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}m(A,x)
\prod_{i=1}^nz_{i,A_i}^{x_i}(1-z_{i,A_i})^{1-x_i}.
\tag{7}
\]
Hence (6) is total and uses only the labels and observed normalizations \(z_{i,A_i}\), never an unobserved potential outcome.

Outcome independence and (5) imply
\[
\mathbb E_\Xi[\tau_c(\Xi)\mid A,y_A]
=\frac1n\sum_{i,a}c_az_{i,a}=d^{-1}\tau_c(y).
\tag{8}
\]
Subtracting (8) from (6) gives
\[
\widehat\tau_I-\tau_c(y)
=d\,\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_{01}(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\mid A,y_A].
\tag{9}
\]
For square-integrable \(W\),
\(\mathbb E[W^2]-(\mathbb E W)^2
=\mathbb E[(W-\mathbb EW)^2]\ge0\).  Applying this elementary identity conditionally in (9), averaging over the assignment, and then using the finite binary support of \(\Xi\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n}\{\widehat\tau_I-\tau_c(y)\}^2
&\le d^2\mathbb E_\Xi
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,\widehat\tau_{01}}
 [\{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\}^2\mid\Xi]\\
&\le d^2\max_{b\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,\widehat\tau_{01}}
 [\{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,b_A)-\tau_c(b)\}^2].
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
This is uniform in \(y\).  Taking the interval supremum and the same estimator and design infima proves the reverse of (4).  All arguments are pointwise in \(A\), so boundary allocations and dependent assignments are included.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the unrestricted two-arm finite-population game, where the infimum ranges over every assignment mechanism and estimator, the binary value is \(\rho_n^\star\); for every fixed finite pair \(L<U\), the bounded-endpoint value is \((U-L)^2\rho_n^\star\); and
\[
\rho_n^\star=\frac1n-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]

added_lemmas.statement:
Restricting the three-arm nature class at \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) to schedules satisfying \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) for every \(i\) gives
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\ge\rho_n^\star
=\frac1n-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Moreover, \(C_A>C_A(5/8)^{2/3}=\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\), so this imported two-arm converse is strictly weaker than the sharp three-arm converse.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
On the restricted class,
\[
\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)
=\frac1n\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(2)/4-3Y_i(3)/4\}
=\frac1n\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(2)\}.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus the target is exactly the two-arm average effect.  Fix any outcome-independent three-arm law and randomized estimator, and put \(B_i=\mathbf1\{A_i=1\}\).  The induced law of \(B\) is an admissible outcome-independent two-arm design.  For each positive-probability \(b\), let \(Q(a\mid b)=\mathbb P(A=a\mid B=b)\).  After observing the binary labels and outcomes, a randomized two-arm estimator can sample \(\widetilde A\sim Q(\cdot\mid B)\) and feed the refined labels and the same outcomes to the three-arm estimator.  Since arms two and three have identical outcomes on the restricted class, this reproduces exactly the original joint law of labels, observations, action, and target.  Zero-probability \(b\)'s are immaterial.  Therefore every three-arm procedure's maximum risk on the restricted class is at least \(\rho_n^\star\).  Restricting nature and then taking the three-arm procedure infimum proves \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge\rho_n^\star\).

The cited two-arm result supplies the expansion.  The exact-primitives proposition and Airy definition give \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\).  Since \(C_A>0\) and \(0<5/8<1\),
\[
C_A-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A\{1-(5/8)^{2/3}\}>0.
\tag{12}
\]
The unequal-three-arm sharp-limit theorem supplies the matching lower expansion with coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).  Subtracting the larger coefficient \(C_A\) gives a strictly smaller asymptotic lower bound, proving the claimed weakness.

proposed.construction:
Let \(\mathcal Y\) be either \(\{0,1\}\) or \([L,U]\) with fixed real \(L<U\), and let \(\mathfrak D_n\) be a nonempty class of assignment laws on \(\mathcal A_K^n\), every member of which is chosen independently of the potential-outcome schedule.  Define
\[
R_{n,\mathcal Y}^{\mathfrak D}(c)
=\inf_{\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D_n,\,\widehat\tau}
\sup_{y\in\mathcal Y^{n\times K}}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,\widehat\tau}\!\left[
\left\{\widehat\tau((A_i,y_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n)
-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_ay_{i,a}
\right\}^2\right],
\]
where \(\widehat\tau\) ranges over all possibly randomized Markov kernels from the labeled observations to \(\mathbb R\).  The displayed linear expression defines \(\tau_c(y)\) on the indicated support and agrees with the frozen causal estimand on binary schedules.  For the class of all outcome-independent laws write \(R_{n,[L,U]}(c)\) on interval schedules.  For the singleton product law with probabilities \(q^\star\), write \(R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)\).  Agreement of a binary specialization with a frozen game whose action space is \([-1,1]\) is a separate projection fact, not part of this definition.

proposed.statement:
For every fixed permitted \(c\), the estimator \(\delta_n^\star\) is total and there is a finite \(B_c\) such that
\[
\max_y\mathbb E[(\delta_n^\star-\tau_c(y))^2]
\le\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}.
\]
The fixed-independent binary risk satisfies
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
=\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
For every fixed real \(L<U\), its bounded-outcome counterpart satisfies
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
=(U-L)^2\left\{\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\right\}.
\]
The Rao--Blackwellized latent-Bernoulli lift \(\delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star\) is total and has maximum risk at most
\[
(U-L)^2\left\{\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}\right\}.
\]
proposed.justification: It converts the dual score and Airy feedback into total full-label finite-data procedures and fixes both the binary and bounded-endpoint independent benchmarks sharply.
proposed.gap: The theorem is sharp for the fixed independent design for every permitted contrast; unrestricted design optimality is proved elsewhere only at the fixed contrast \(c^\dagger\), not for general \(c\).
proposed.consumer: A prospective binary or bounded-endpoint multiarm trial can implement the independent benchmark and its explicit Rao--Blackwellized interval-valued lift.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The active maximality directive explicitly adds the exact bounded-endpoint expansion and attaining lift to this owned theorem and attaches the reduction to its proof spine.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), and for every fixed \(L<U\), \(R_{n,[L,U]}(c^\dagger)=(U-L)^2\{n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\}\); the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) attains the same binary and bounded second-order values, while the terminating exact finite-data evaluator is asserted only for the binary game.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline functional must include the exact bounded-endpoint corollary while preserving the binary-only scope of the computable finite certificate.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.2 gives the unrestricted two-arm binary game, Theorem 2.3 gives exact bounded-endpoint scaling, and Theorem 3.1 gives \(\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\).
Theorem 1 optimizes over every two-arm assignment mechanism and measurable estimator and gives the equivalent exact bounded-endpoint game.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The unrestricted three-arm equality and exact bounded lift now extend the two-arm comparator promises; the corrected Sudijono theorem numbering separates equality, scaling, and the Airy expansion.

prose_updates.tldr: For the fixed unequal contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the unrestricted binary three-arm minimax risk is now proved to satisfy \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), and the independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) attains the same second-order value. The face-robust all-count argument supplies the matching all-procedure lower bound, while the binary evaluator returns terminating finite risk brackets and a total procedure. An exact finite-sample Rao--Blackwell reduction further gives \(R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathfrak D}(c)=(U-L)^2R_{n,\{0,1\}}^{\mathfrak D}(c)\) for every fixed bounded interval and every fixed class of outcome-independent designs. The remaining sharpness limitation is unrestricted design optimality for general contrasts \(c\), not the fixed contrast \(c^\dagger\).

project_justification.gap: Published exact unrestricted results cover the binary-treatment action space. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen optimize jointly over all binary-treatment assignment laws and estimators, and Hull gives the equivalent all-mechanism bounded two-arm game; neither treats a three-arm action space. The accepted parent established only the first-order value and the order of the second-order gain. The present result closes the sharp coefficient at the fixed unequal three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger\), while the same unrestricted conclusion for a general permitted contrast remains open.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), the exact eight-response-type geometry and the three-coordinate face-robust prior cover local allocations, positive-count exterior allocations, and every zero-count face without an overlap assumption. This yields an unrestricted three-arm coefficient \(C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), proves that \(q^\dagger\) has no second-order loss there, and separates that result from the strictly weaker two-arm nature restriction with coefficient \(C_A\).
project_justification.fill: The contribution combines a total independent Airy-feedback procedure, an exact-target generalized van Trees lower ledger uniform over all allocation counts, a computable nonincreasing finite-to-limit tail, and a terminating binary finite-data evaluator. The bounded-endpoint reduction is exact for each finite \(n\): endpoint inclusion proves one direction, and latent Bernoulli completion followed by conditional Jensen proves the other without changing the design class or estimator quantifiers. It transfers both the unrestricted \(c^\dagger\) theorem and the fixed-independent general-contrast theorem to every fixed interval \([L,U]\).

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including arbitrary dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. At \(c^\dagger\), the proved all-count converse matches the total procedure under independent \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\). The bounded-support corollary preserves the chosen design-law class exactly.
sampling_model.units: The kernel is a fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes and all eight response types. For outcomes in a fixed interval \([L,U]\), the causal contrast and minimax risk are transferred from the binary game by the exact latent-Bernoulli reduction; no superpopulation sampling is introduced.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed. The common-shift tangent supplies a target-changing direction invisible on every proper allocation face, and the proved local, exterior, and zero-face inequalities make the all-design lower expansion uniform over every allocation count.

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 2.2, optimize over every assignment mechanism and estimator in the binary-treatment finite-population game; Theorem 2.3 proves exact bounded-endpoint scaling, and Theorem 3.1 proves \(\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). Hull (2026), version 3, Theorem 1, likewise optimizes over every assignment mechanism and measurable estimator and gives the equivalent exact bounded two-arm game. Neither paper covers a three-arm action space. Restricting the present nature class to \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) gives the valid comparison \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), but \(C_A>C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), so that imported converse is strictly weaker than the proved three-arm coefficient. Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) impose different model, asymptotic, or estimator restrictions. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) provide limiting-decision and spectral context. Hammer et al. (1996) is only motivation for a prospective complete fixed-horizon binary-endpoint regimen trial; no censored ACTG175 outcome is reanalyzed.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a prospective three-regimen trial with the fixed contrast \(c^\dagger\), a trialist may prespecify independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) and the total Airy-feedback procedure knowing that no outcome-independent dependent design and no possibly biased labeled-data estimator improves its second-order minimax coefficient. The binary evaluator supplies finite risk brackets and an all-future error certificate. If all potential outcomes instead lie in a fixed interval \([L,U]\), the explicit latent-Bernoulli conditional-expectation lift is a total procedure and multiplies the corresponding binary minimax risk by \((U-L)^2\). This is a prospective design result, not a reanalysis of censored ACTG175 data.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Unrestricted sharpness is proved only for the fixed rational contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\). For every permitted fixed real contrast, the fixed-independent expansion and its exact bounded-endpoint lift are proved, but equality with the unrestricted design game is not claimed. The terminating same-input evaluator remains a binary, fixed-rational-contrast certificate; the analytic bounded-endpoint reduction does not by itself provide a rational encoding for arbitrary real endpoints or contrasts. No growing-\(K\), uniform vanishing-weight, or arbitrary-real computability statement is made. The finite \(K=3,n=3\) label gap remains diagnostic rather than an asymptotic argument.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the unrestricted sharp binary expansion and equality of the independent second-order value at \(c^\dagger\), together with a terminating binary finite-to-limit certificate. It also proves the exact bounded-endpoint scaling for every fixed interval and every fixed outcome-independent design-law class, so both the unrestricted \(c^\dagger\) result and the general-contrast fixed-independent result have bounded-outcome corollaries. The exact eight-type kernel and effective evaluator remain explicitly binary. Unrestricted sharpness for contrasts other than \(c^\dagger\), growing numbers of arms, uniform vanishing weights, and computation from an unrepresented arbitrary real contrast are outside the claim.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem turns the response-alphabet dual score and Airy feedback into total labeled-data procedures, proves the fixed-independent binary coefficient for every permitted contrast, and transfers the result exactly to fixed endpoints.
statement_notes.gap: Its design is fixed at \(q^\star\); unrestricted optimality for general \(c\) is not inferred from the theorem, although it is separately proved at \(c^\dagger\).
statement_notes.consumer: A prospective binary or fixed bounded-endpoint multiarm trial can implement the independent benchmark and its explicit Rao--Blackwellized lift.

proofs.proof_tex:
The exact-primitives proposition gives
\(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\) and identifies
\(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\) for every labeled schedule in the response-count orbit.  The Airy definition therefore gives
\[
 \Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\tag{12}
\]
For every sufficiently large \(n\), the allocation-tube theorem supplies the live positivity certificate
\[
 \alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})
 \le\frac12,
\tag{13}
\]
the exact-target all-count bounds \({\rm(A)}\), the feasible total procedure in \({\rm(B)}\), and the common tail modulus in \({\rm(C)}\).  In particular the face-robust prior is supported on probability laws.  The exact-target directional van Trees ledger and the permutation-orbit Bayes lemma therefore apply to the random finite-population target itself, rather than merely to its conditional mean.  For an arbitrary outcome-independent, possibly dependent design with allocation-count law \(\pi\), and for every randomized labeled-data estimator, the orbit lemma gives
\[
 \operatorname{BR}
 \ge\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
       \mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{14}
\]
The first inequality uses outcome independence, and the second uses
\(\sum_r\pi(r)=1\) and the definition of \(B^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) as the minimum over all allocation counts.  Maximum risk is at least Bayes risk under every prior, so taking the infimum over all admissible designs and estimators in \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\) proves
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)
 \ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{15}
\]

By the exact Bayes-risk definition,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}
 -B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
 &=n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}
 -\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 \mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\right\}\\
 &=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]
The sets \(\mathcal L_n\), \(\mathcal X_n\), and \(\mathcal Z_n\) are disjoint and exhaust \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\).  Hence conclusion \({\rm(A)}\), applied in the appropriate stratum in \((16)\), yields, with
\(e_n^-=\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\}\),
\[
 B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
 \ge \frac1n-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-)n^{-4/3}.
\tag{17}
\]
Conclusion \({\rm(B)}\) supplies a total feasible estimator
\(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\), so the defining minimax infimum and that conclusion give
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)
 \le \max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
   \{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
 \le \frac1n-(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n})n^{-4/3}.
\tag{18}
\]
Equations \((15)\), \((17)\), and \((18)\) prove the complete chain in equation \((1)\) of the theorem and, after rearrangement,
\[
 \Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
 \le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
 \le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{19}
\]
For every \(N\) after the finite startup and every \(n\ge N\), conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) bounds both \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\) and \(e_n^-\) by \(E(N)\).  Thus \((19)\) implies
\[
 \left|n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
 -\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\right|\le E(N).
\tag{20}
\]
Since \(E(N)\downarrow0\), equation \((20)\), followed by multiplication by \(n^{-4/3}\), proves
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)
 =\frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Together with \((12)\), this proves every clause of the target.  The argument uses only the live face-robust positivity condition \((13)\), the exact finite-population target Bayes reduction, and conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\); it does not invoke the obsolete scalar prior or an existential primal remainder.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(K\) and \(n\) be fixed, let \(L<U\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^K\) satisfy \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_a=0\), and let \(\mathfrak D_n\) be any nonempty fixed class of outcome-independent assignment laws, with arbitrary dependence among the unit assignments allowed.  Then
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)
 =(U-L)^2R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c).
\tag{BE}
\]
If also \(\sum_a|c_a|=2\), then for the unrestricted design class \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)=R_n(c)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(d=U-L>0\).  We prove the two inequalities in \((\mathrm{BE})\) without changing either the design class or the estimator quantifier.

For the lower bound, every endpoint schedule has the form
\(w_{i,a}=L+d x_{i,a}\) with
\(x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}\).  The zero-sum condition gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \tau_c(w)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i,a}c_a(L+d x_{i,a})
 =L\sum_a c_a+d\tau_c(x)
 =d\tau_c(x).
\tag{3}
\]
Given any design \(\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D_n\) and any bounded-outcome procedure \(\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}\), rescaling its kernel by
\[
 \widehat\tau_{01}(A,x_A)
 =d^{-1}\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}(A,L+d x_A)
\]
produces an admissible binary procedure under the same design.  By \((3)\), its risk at \(x\) is exactly \(d^{-2}\) times the bounded procedure's risk at the associated endpoint schedule.  Taking the binary maximum, then the bounded supremum, and finally the joint infimum gives
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)
 \le d^{-2}R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c).
\tag{4}
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix a design
\(\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D_n\) and a possibly randomized binary procedure \(\widehat\tau_{01}\) having finite worst-case risk; procedures of infinite risk can be discarded because the zero procedure has finite risk.  Let
\[
 m(A,u)=\int r\,\widehat\tau_{01}(dr\mid A,u),
 \qquad u\in\{0,1\}^n,
\]
be its conditional mean.  For a bounded schedule \(w\), put
\(z_{i,a}=(w_{i,a}-L)/d\in[0,1]\).  Define the bounded procedure by the finite formula
\[
 \widehat\tau_{[L,U]}(A,w_A)
 =d\sum_{u\in\{0,1\}^n}m(A,u)
   \prod_{i=1}^n
   z_{i,A_i}^{u_i}(1-z_{i,A_i})^{1-u_i}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus \((5)\) is evaluated from the assignment labels and the observed numbers \(z_{i,A_i}\) only; it contains no unobserved \(z_{i,a}\).

For the risk calculation, independently of \(A\), draw a latent complete binary schedule \(\Xi=(\Xi_{i,a})\) with mutually independent coordinates
\(\Xi_{i,a}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(z_{i,a})\), and include the original procedure's auxiliary randomization in the same conditional expectation.  Outcome independence of every law in \(\mathfrak D_n\) is used here: the law of \(A\) is unchanged by, and independent of, this latent randomization.  Formula \((5)\), zero-sum affine equivariance \((3)\), and
\(\mathbb E_\Xi\tau_c(\Xi)=\tau_c(z)=d^{-1}\tau_c(w)\) yield
\[
 \widehat\tau_{[L,U]}(A,w_A)-\tau_c(w)
 =d\,\mathbb E_\Xi\!\left[
   \widehat\tau_{01}(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)
   \mid A,w_A\right].
\tag{6}
\]
Conditional Jensen's inequality applied to \((6)\), followed by averaging over \(A\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_A\!\left[
   \{\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}-\tau_c(w)\}^2\right]
 &\le d^2\mathbb E_{A,\Xi}\!\left[
   \{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\}^2\right]\\
 &=d^2\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}
   \mathbb P(\Xi=x)
   \mathbb E_A\!\left[
   \{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,x_A)-\tau_c(x)\}^2\right]\\
 &\le d^2\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}
   \mathbb E_A\!\left[
   \{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,x_A)-\tau_c(x)\}^2\right].
 \end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
The equality on the second line uses the independence just stated and is valid for dependent assignments across units.  Taking the supremum over \(w\) and then the infimum over the same admissible binary design--procedure pairs proves
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)
 \le d^2R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c),
\tag{8}
\]
which, with \((4)\), proves \((\mathrm{BE})\).

Finally suppose \(\sum_a|c_a|=2\).  Together with \(\sum_a c_a=0\), this implies
\(\sum_{a:c_a>0}c_a=\sum_{a:c_a<0}|c_a|=1\), so every binary value \(\tau_c(x)\) lies in \([-1,1]\).  Projection of a real-valued action onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase squared distance from such a target.  Hence allowing all real actions in \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)\) has the same value as the action restriction in \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\), proving \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)=R_n(c)\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For the unrestricted two-treatment binary-potential-outcome game with contrast \((1,-1)\), when every assignment mechanism and every measurable possibly randomized estimator are admissible, its minimax risk \(\rho_n^\star\) satisfies
\[
 \rho_n^\star
 =\frac1n-C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]

attestation.note: The orchestrator supplied a direct source audit of arXiv:2608.13822v1, Theorems 2.2--2.3, for the unrestricted binary-treatment quantifiers and Airy expansion; a stable arXiv handle is used because no lawful verbatim transcription was supplied.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
On the displayed submodel write \(x_{i,1}=y_{i,1}\) and
\(x_{i,0}=y_{i,2}=y_{i,3}\).  Direct substitution gives
\[
 \tau_{c^\dagger}(y)
 =\frac1n\sum_i\left(y_{i,1}-\frac14y_{i,2}-\frac34y_{i,3}\right)
 =\frac1n\sum_i(x_{i,1}-x_{i,0}),
\tag{9}
\]
which is the binary causal contrast.

Given any outcome-independent three-arm design, define the binary label
\(B_i=1\) if \(A_i=1\) and \(B_i=0\) if \(A_i\in\{2,3\}\).  The induced law of \(B\) is outcome-independent and may have arbitrary cross-unit dependence.  Conditional on \(B\), the residual distinction between labels two and three has a distribution fixed by the design and independent of the schedule.  Therefore a binary estimator can reproduce the risk of any three-arm estimator on the submodel by drawing \(A\) from its design-known conditional law given \(B\) and then applying the three-arm estimator.  The extra label is thus only admissible auxiliary randomization.  This maps every three-arm design--estimator pair to a binary pair with the same risk, and hence the binary minimax value is no larger than the restricted three-arm value.

Conversely, any binary assignment law is embedded in the three-arm problem by assigning arm one when \(B_i=1\) and arm two when \(B_i=0\), never assigning arm three, and using the binary estimator.  Equation \((9)\) then makes the risks identical, so the restricted three-arm value is no larger than the binary value.  The two values are equal.  Since the maximum over all three-arm schedules is at least the maximum over this submodel for every design--estimator pair, taking infima proves the first inequality in \((\mathrm{TA})\).  The cited two-arm Airy theorem supplies the expansion for \(\rho_n^\star\).  Finally, \(C_A>0\) and \(0<5/8<1\) imply
\[
 C_A-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}=C_A\{1-(5/8)^{2/3}\}>0,
\]
which proves the strict second-order comparison.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every pair of fixed real endpoints \(L<U\), the unrestricted outcome-independent three-arm game with potential outcomes in \([L,U]\) satisfies
\[
 R_{n,[L,U]}(c^\dagger)
 =(U-L)^2\left\{
 \frac1n-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})
 \right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
The finite eight-response-type allocation-tube construction remains a binary certificate; equation \((10)\) is its exact bounded-endpoint consequence.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) has zero sum and \(\ell^1\)-norm two.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:multiarm\text{-}bounded\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) with \(\mathfrak D_n\) equal to the class of all outcome-independent three-arm assignment laws.  It gives the exact finite-sample identity
\[
 R_{n,[L,U]}(c^\dagger)
 =(U-L)^2R_n(c^\dagger).
\tag{11}
\]
Substitute the sharp binary expansion from
\(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}sharp\text{-}limit}\) into \((11)\).  Because \(L\) and \(U\) are fixed, multiplication of its remainder by the fixed number \((U-L)^2\) preserves the order \(o(n^{-4/3})\).  This proves \((10)\) without modifying the binary allocation-tube construction or its finite evaluator.

proposed.name: Fixed-class bounded-outcome minimax game
proposed.construction:
Fix real endpoints \(L<U\), and let \(\mathfrak D=(\mathfrak D_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a sequence such that \(\mathfrak D_n\) is a nonempty class of assignment laws on \(\mathcal A_K^n\), fixed without reference to the potential-outcome schedule.  For \(w=(w_{i,a})\in[L,U]^{n\times K}\), define
\[
 \tau_c(w)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_aw_{i,a}.
\]
With \(W_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=w_{i,A_i}\), define the fixed-design-class bounded-outcome game by
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)
 =\inf_{\substack{\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D_n\\
                   \widehat\tau\text{ a Markov kernel}}}
   \sup_{w\in[L,U]^{n\times K}}
   \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n}\!\left[
      \left\{\widehat\tau((A_i,W_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^n)
      -\tau_c(w)\right\}^2\right],
\]
where the kernel may take values in \(\mathbb R\), and the expectation includes its internal randomization.  Write \(R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)\) for the analogous game with schedules in \(\{0,1\}^{n\times K}\).  When \(\mathfrak D_n\) is the class of all outcome-independent assignment laws, omit the superscript and write \(R_{n,[L,U]}(c)\) and \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact bounded-endpoint lift must be stated as a design-based minimax game before its scale identity can be proved.
